name: One-Handed
governs: damage, poise damage and stamina cost of swords, axes, maces and daggers held in one hand
description: The Vale's fighting is done with tools that were something else first. A sword is a scythe that learned manners.

name: Two-Handed
governs: damage, poise damage and stamina cost of greatswords, spears and great hammers
description: Weight, committed. The Tolling Order trains it in silence, because a blade that long says enough.

name: Archery
governs: bow and crossbow damage, draw speed and steadiness at full draw
description: The Woodfolk's whole law is a bow. Skerrow's chain-bridge guards would add: and a crosswind.

name: Block
governs: shield and weapon stability, the stamina cost of taking a hit on guard, and the parry window
description: Standing where you were put. Wardens paint their family's door-colour on the shield so everyone knows who did.

name: Armour
governs: how much worn armour protects and how little it slows and quietens you
description: Clan plate is heavy because bone remembers standing up. Learning to wear it is learning to agree with it.

name: Sneak
governs: visibility, movement noise, sneak-attack damage, pickpocketing and lockpicking
description: The Quiet Hands teach that the unsaid is safer than the untrue. Their ledger is the only honest book in Tollmere.

name: Speech
governs: prices, persuasion, intimidation and how quickly your deeds are talked about
description: In a world where being spoken of keeps you warm, talk is not cheap. It is the whole economy.

name: Alchemy
governs: potion and poison potency and the discovery of ingredient effects
description: Hedge-wisdom written down. Every ingredient has four things to say; it tells you the first and makes you earn the rest.

name: Smithing
governs: what you can forge and how far you can temper what you own
description: Red-door work. Vale smiths stamp a bell on every ingot so the iron knows where it is from and comes back when called.

name: Enchanting
governs: the strength and charge of notes written into gear at a Name-table
description: To enchant is to write a word into a thing so it holds. Ember Motes are the ink; the Builders' whole city was the first draft.

name: Athletics
governs: sprinting, dodging, jumping, swimming and carrying
description: The Reedfolk swim before they walk. The clans run chain bridges in the wind. The Vale mostly walks to the inn, but briskly.

name: Kindling
governs: Saying of fire and light: spell power and mana cost, and the capture of Ember Motes
description: The Candle account made practical. Say a thing warmly enough and it burns.

name: Hush
governs: Saying of frost, silence and concealment: spell power and mana cost
description: The Hushline taught this school by example. Cold, quiet, and gone before it is mentioned.

name: Binding
governs: Saying of wards, shields and snares: spell power, duration and mana cost
description: Oroth grammar, half-understood. A ward is a sentence that refuses to end.

name: Mending
governs: Saying that heals and cleanses: spell power and mana cost
description: Tending, spoken aloud. The Vale says every hearth-mother knows one Mending word and will not tell you which.

name: Calling
governs: Saying that summons and animates: spell power, duration and mana cost
description: Naming something so firmly it has to come. The Sayers' Circle teaches it last, and to few, and shares its practice with Mending: both are the same word said in different weather.
